facts.statement: The genus Ischyrhiza was first described by Leidy in 1856.
The type species of the genus Ischyrhiza is Ischyrhiza mira.
The genus Ischyrhiza was originally placed under the authority of Cope in 1875.
Ischyrhiza belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Ischyrhiza is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Ischyrhiza lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Cenomanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Ischyrhiza is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid ray from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian-Maastrichtian).

facts.statement: Ischyrhiza possessed a large, toothed rostrum that closely resembled that of a modern sawfish.
facts.quote: It had a large, toothed rostrum closely resembling that of a modern-day sawfish.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ischyrhiza have been discovered in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Uzbekistan, Japan, Niger, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.
facts.quote: Fossils of the genus have been found in Canada, the United States, the Aguja Formation of Mexico, the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan, the Tamayama Formation of Japan, the Dukamaje Formation of Niger, the El Molino Formation of Bolivia, the Quiriquina Formation of Chile, and the Chota Formation of Peru.

facts.statement: The time range for Ischyrhiza spans from the Albian to the Thanetian, approximately 113.2 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Thanetian (113.2 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest that Ischyrhiza, along with Schizorhiza and Onchopristis, forms a distinct clade closer to the extant family Rajidae (true skates), which may render the suborder Sclerorhynchoidei paraphyletic.
facts.quote: Despite formerly being classified within a family of extinct sawfish-like rays known as Sclerorhynchidae, phylogenetic analyses indicate that Ischyrhiza, Schizorhiza, and Onchopristis form a distinct clade that groups closer with the extant family Rajidae, which contains the true skates, possibly rendering the suborder Sclerorhynchoidei paraphyletic.
